question.text: Lotus Capital AIF's compliance officer is preparing the FY 2024-25 tax reporting. Which of the following pairings of form and deadline is CORRECT for an Investment Fund under the ITA?

answer.text: Form 64C to the jurisdictional Commissioner by 31 July; Form 64D to LPs by 15 June.

Form 64C to each LP by 30 June of the following FY; Form 64D electronically to the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner / Commissioner by 15 June of the following FY (digitally signed, verified by a practising CA).
Form 64A to LPs by 31 March; Form 64B to SEBI by 31 May.
Form 26AS by 30 April for all LPs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the reporting-compliance provisions in Chapter 13: Form 64C — a statement of income paid/credited to each unitholder — must be furnished to the LP by 30 JUNE of the following FY. Form 64D — a similar statement furnished ELECTRONICALLY to the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner / Commissioner — is due by 15 JUNE of the following FY, digitally signed and verified by a practising CA. Missing these triggers penalties and LP-service issues. The Trap: Option A inverts the recipients and deadlines. Option C invents Forms 64A/64B which don't exist in this context. Option D confuses Form 26AS (a portal-generated tax-credit statement for any taxpayer) with the AIF-specific Forms 64C/64D. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same Form 64C/64D deadlines. XIX-A tests it at the distributor level (LPs ask their RMs when to expect the form). InvITs/REITs have parallel Form 64A/64B — do NOT confuse the two regimes. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a 'Form 64C/64D calendar' into your compliance tracker: CA sign-off by 10 June, Form 64D filing by 15 June, Form 64C mailing to LPs by 30 June. A delayed Form 64C is the #1 LP complaint that escalates to the GP — get ahead of it.
